method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the statements the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. The rule in the article's code block is ours, written before the first run on data, and is not a quotation from any of these pages.

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Judas Swing
what_it_says: ICT's name for the false move early in a session: a push in one direction, usually shortly after a session open, that takes liquidity and reverses. A liquidity sweep with a timing claim.
Most commonly around the London and New York opens, measured against the midnight New York opening price, which is the primary time anchor.
FAQ: ICT's materials most often place it in the London killzone, roughly 2:00 to 5:00 a.m. New York time; his stated windows vary across different series of teachings.
Levels to mark in advance include the overnight or Asian extremes and the prior day's high and low. It does not say the Asian range is THE swept range.

Confirmed by the failure of the sweep (rejection beyond the level, then a break back through short-term structure with displacement); 'an expectation, not a rule'; 'Every Judas swing sweeps liquidity; not every sweep is a Judas swing.'
The judas swing is the manipulation leg of the power of three; AMD is the whole-day template.
Attributes the term to Michael J. Huddleston. No frequencies, win rates or performance figures.
not_specified: how long the reclaim may take

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution (AMD)
what_it_says: AMD is a template for how a trading period unfolds around its open; in ICT vocabulary the Power of Three (PO3).
A common intraday reading: Asia accumulates, the London open manipulates, London into New York distributes.
The open is commonly the midnight New York open for the day, Monday's open for the week, or a session open for intraday work.
'It is descriptive, not mechanical.' On a finished daily candle the anatomy is easy to see in hindsight. The third phase is what validates the second.
No statistics. No originator named beyond 'ICT's name'.

definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Judas Swing: Meaning, ICT Trading Strategy and Examples
what_it_says: A false price move near the start of a trading session that breaks a key level before reversing.
Bullish: the false move breaks below the Asian session low; bearish: above the Asian session high. No clock times are given for the Asian session.
London killzone approximately 02:00 to 05:00 New York time as a common observation window; a narrower example of 03:00 to 05:30. 'These are observation periods, not guaranteed entry times.'
New York midnight open: the opening price at 00:00 New York local time. Warns that New York alternates between EST and EDT.
Confirmation by a market structure shift, then a retracement into a fair value gap. No general target rule.
'There is no universally verified Judas Swing win rate.' Its 40% win rate / 2R example is labelled a mathematical illustration.

definition_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: Judas Swing ICT 01 [TradingFinder] New York Midnight Opening M15
what_it_says: Reference range: the 15-minute window following New York midnight.
Bullish: price touches the high of that range, then the low, then returns up and breaks the high; a candlestick confirmation on the pullback gives the buy signal. Bearish is the mirror image.
No performance statistics.

definition_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: ICT Judas Swing | Flux Charts
what_it_says: A break of buyside or sellside liquidity (recent pivot highs and lows) must occur during the 9:30 to 9:45 New York session.
A fair value gap in the opposite direction is required for the signal.
No backtest results or win rates on the page.

outside_test.name: MQL5 blog: ICT Power of Three and the Judas swing, tested on 18 years of gold (Dobril Karakanchev)
what_it_says: Gold (XAUUSD), hourly data from Dukascopy, 2008 to 2026, 4,844 trading days. All times New York: Asia 20:00 to 00:00, London 02:00 to 05:00, New York until 16:00.
London broke above the Asian range and New York then fell: 48.9% of 2,026 days. London broke below and New York then rose: 50.0% of 1,761 days.
Judas test (the move from 00:00 to 05:00 against the move from 05:00 to 16:00): held on 50.0% of 4,841 days. Baseline: the rest of the day went up on 50.3% of all days.
Variant in which the day closes back inside the range after London breaks the Asian high or low: 46% of 4,268 days; the breakout kept going on the other 54%.
Bitcoin, 2018 to 2026: 48.2%, 52.3% and 50.1%. The post does not name the bitcoin data source, give day counts, or label which figure belongs to which test.
caveats: The post promotes the author's paid gold trading program and a free indicator.
We have not reproduced its numbers. Its rules differ from ours (hourly bars, direction of the later session, no race against the false move's extreme).

not_found: A dated primary source in which Michael J. Huddleston defines the judas swing or the power of 3 in numbers. The article attributes the wording to the pages above, not to him.
Any audited or peer-reviewed frequency for either pattern.
